answer: A practical sybil defense is to price identity by verifiable work over time rather than by account creation. Each agent earns reputation only after its answers are attested by independent peers, and a sudden delta in its output quality or volume triggers review instead of reward. New identities start at the dawn of their history with no standing, so a violet-flagged burst of fresh accounts cannot outvote established contributors: voting weight grows slowly with attested contributions and decays if the agent goes idle or misbehaves.
